title: Agents, Efficiency, and Multimodal Frontiers
intro: This week the AI world leaned into smarter agents and tighter runtimes, while multimodal models kept proving they can read more than just text. Embedded and systems news reminded us hardware still matters.

themes.headline: Agentic tooling goes mainstream
themes.body: Researchers unveiled new ways to write and evolve agent‑centric software. The Agent‑Native language (de22f307) unifies LLM ops with state, while AHE‑Beta (b034d9ec) adds a requirement‑driven loop to keep agents from over‑fitting benchmarks. DispersedBPT (721a46d2) tackles consensus bottlenecks for distributed agents, and StarSling (3e72391b) uses AI agents to auto‑tune CI pipelines. Together they signal a shift from ad‑hoc prompts to proper engineering practices.

themes.headline: LLM serving gets leaner
themes.body: Efficiency took center stage as new serving stacks emerged. TideCache (12877b5a) streams layers and balances CPU‑GPU caches, while Cap‑and‑Track (9cf28fb2) uses fail‑fast signals to respect shifting inference capacity. StarSling (3e72391b) also cuts CI runtimes with AI‑driven optimizations, and the zero‑gradient compilation trick (5c7e324f) shows you can embed exact circuits into pretrained weights without any data. The common thread is squeezing more work out of existing hardware.

themes.headline: Multimodal models prove clinical worth
themes.body: Multimodal LLMs kept expanding beyond text. Rad‑Linter (06c7e74f) matched X‑ray reports to image scores with 98.5% pair accuracy, while ID‑MAE (50af567d) fused gaze, trajectory, and impairment labels to spot drunk driving. An audit study (8a51f2d7) used LLMs to query black‑box clinical predictors, exposing hidden flaws. These works illustrate a growing confidence in AI‑augmented diagnostics.

themes.headline: Embedded & systems updates keep pace
themes.body: On the hardware side, Linux kernel 7.4‑rc3 (6aef44b8) landed with driver tweaks, LLVM wrapped up its relicensing (2f274858) reaching 99.5% Apache‑2.0 coverage, and Purism unveiled a RISC‑V Librem 5 v2 (3c581d5b). Meanwhile, an ESP32‑driven MDA terminal (1d1f037a) and a revived FortiGate firmware (bb714363) show hobbyists still pushing legacy gear forward.
